en: Morning dew on banana leaves is liquid water that condensed from invisible water vapor gas in the cool air.
Seawater in Manila Bay is a homogeneous mixture where solid salt is completely dissolved in liquid water.
Reddish-brown rust on old jeepney parts forms when iron metal chemically reacts with oxygen and moisture in air.
Puddles on a school driveway disappear as liquid water physically changes into invisible water vapor gas under the sun.
Pumice stones found near Taal Volcano float on water because this porous volcanic rock is less dense than liquid.
Making tuba involves a chemical change where microorganisms convert the liquid sugar in coconut sap into alcohol and gas.
Muddy river water after heavy rain is a heterogeneous mixture where solid soil particles are suspended in liquid.
Invisible water vapor gas released by plants condenses into liquid droplets on the inside of a plastic bag.
Crushing dried fish into smaller pieces changes its physical size and shape but does not alter its chemical composition.
Iron-rich black sand on Ilocos beaches is strongly attracted to a magnet because it contains the magnetic metal iron.
Burning dried rice hulls into ash is a chemical change because the solid material reacts with oxygen to form new substances.
Calamansi powder dissolves faster in warm water than in cold water because higher temperatures increase the liquid solvent molecules' movement.
